_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader). Africa-branch municipal-fiscal-tier push, round AF/G.23, 2026-08-13. First municipal/regional-tier findings for Namibia — existing corpus (na-cpi-social-protection.json) was national-CPI/pension-and-social-protection only. This round mints Namibia's two foundational local-government finance statutes (Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992, with its named 5%-of-property-rates municipal-to-regional transfer formula at s.77, and the parallel Regional Councils Act 22 of 1992) plus the City of Windhoek's own Strategic Plan 2022-2027, which states the capital's dependency on national-government funding/tax-sharing in its own words. A near-total pattern of `.gov.na` domain unreachability (TLS resets and HTTP 503s across oag.gov.na, murd.gov.na, mof.gov.na, www.gov.na, and npc.gov.na's https endpoint) blocked verification of the Auditor-General's named local-authority audit reports and the Ministry of Urban and Rural Development's budget speech this round — recorded as a corpus/system observation below, not as confirmed content absence. No named equalisation/compensation fund (the Namibian analogue to Mozambique's FCA or Angola's FEAL) was found in either statute after full-text search of both.

reports.title: Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992
reports.publisher: Government of the Republic of Namibia
reports.description: Namibia's foundational statute governing local authority councils (municipalities, towns and villages, e.g. Windhoek, Walvis Bay, Swakopmund), including their finances. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this round via the Legal Assistance Centre's Annotated Statutes edition -- a verbatim reproduction (with bracketed amendment annotations) of the Government Gazette Act text, not an NGO paraphrase. Section 77(1)-(2), Part XVI, establishes the clearest documented municipal-to-regional fiscal-transfer formula found in the Namibian corpus to date: 'There shall be levied for the benefit of the funds of regional councils an amount equal to five per cent of the rates levied under section 73 on all rateable property situated in local authority areas. ... The amount referred to in subsection (1) shall be collected by a local authority council situated in the region of the regional council concerned in such manner as may be determined by the Minister and paid over to the regional council on such date or dates as may be so determined.' Section 80(1), Part XVII ('Financial Matters'), defines a local authority council's own funds: 'The funds of a local authority council shall consist of - (a) moneys appropriated by law for purposes of the funds of the local authority council; (b) the rates, charges, fees and other moneys levied under any provision of this Act and received by the local authority council; ...' -- establishing, without naming a specific grant/subsidy scheme, that local authorities' funds may include national-law appropriations. Hosting caveat: this copy is hosted by the Legal Assistance Centre (lac.org.na), a Namibian NGO, not a .gov.na domain -- every .gov.na domain tested this round (including npc.gov.na) either TLS-reset mid-handshake or returned HTTP 503/404, so no working government-hosted mirror of this Act could be confirmed this round; the LAC copy is a verbatim annotated reproduction of the Act of Parliament text, not a paraphrase.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, currently in force per this annotated compilation.

reports.title: Regional Councils Act 22 of 1992
reports.publisher: Government of the Republic of Namibia
reports.description: Namibia's foundational statute governing regional councils' establishment and finances. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this round: the government-agency host (National Planning Commission, npc.gov.na) copy returned a TLS certificate error ('unable to get local issuer certificate') under both curl and WebFetch, so text was extracted from an identical mirror (confirmed by diff against the npc.gov.na copy's accessible metadata) hosted by the Legal Assistance Centre. Section 33(1), Part VIII ('Financial Matters'), defines a regional council's funds: '33. (1) The funds of a regional council shall consist of - (a) moneys appropriated by law for purposes of the funds of the regional council; (b) the rates, charges, fees and other moneys levied and received by the regional council under any provision of this Act in respect of immovable property situated within a settlement area in its region and services rendered by it or the regulation and control of any matter in a settlement area; (c) any moneys borrowed by the regional council by way of loans or the issue of debentures, bills of exchange or other negotiable instruments; ... (g) any moneys accruing to the funds of the regional council from any other source.' A full-text search of the entire extracted Act (2,740 lines) for 'equalis-', 'equaliz-', 'grant', 'subsid-' and 'Development Fund' found no named equalisation/compensation fund -- the Namibian analogue to Mozambique's FCA or Angola's FEAL does not exist in this Act -- the closest functional mechanism is the flat 5%-of-rates remittance from local authorities under the Local Authorities Act s.77 (na-local-authorities-act-1992).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, currently in force per this annotated compilation.

reports.title: City of Windhoek Strategic Plan 2022-2027
reports.publisher: City of Windhoek (Municipal Council of Windhoek)
reports.description: The City of Windhoek's own strategic plan, its primary self-published municipal planning document. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this round. Table 3 ('Sustainable City Concept Descriptions', p.12) states the City's own funding strategy: 'Sustain ourselves through revenue and tax sharing and funding from the Government of the Republic of Namibia for CAPEX, Safety, Early Childhood Development, and social projects.' The strategic risk register (p.26, 'Enhance Financial Sustainability' objective, Risk #3) names a specific financial risk: 'Inadequate funding provided by the central government to subsidise basic services,' with stated impact 'Unable to deliver basic services such as water, electricity, sanitation, and housing amongst others.' Neither passage names a specific enabling statute, grant scheme, or formula for this national-government funding/tax-sharing -- the dependency on the 'Government of the Republic of Namibia' is stated by the City in its own words but is not tied by this document to any named instrument (e.g. the Local Authorities Act's general appropriations clause, s.80(1)(a)), so no citation-based edge to a specific national statute is drawn from this document (see _dropped).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational municipal planning document covering the 2022-2027 cycle.

dependencies.basis: Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992, s.77(1)-(2): 'There shall be levied for the benefit of the funds of regional councils an amount equal to five per cent of the rates levied under section 73 on all rateable property situated in local authority areas. ... The amount referred to in subsection (1) shall be collected by a local authority council situated in the region of the regional council concerned ... and paid over to the regional council.' A regional council's funds under Regional Councils Act s.33(1)(a) ('moneys appropriated by law for purposes of the funds of the regional council') include this amount, which is mechanically computed as a fixed 5% of the local-authority property rates levied under the Local Authorities Act s.73 -- the clearest documented municipal-to-regional fiscal-transfer formula found in this round's research.

_dropped.edge: na-regional-councils-act-1992 -> named equalisation/compensation fund (Namibian analogue to Mozambique's FCA / Angola's FEAL)
_dropped.why: Full-text search of both the Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992 (7,110 lines extracted) and the Regional Councils Act 22 of 1992 (2,740 lines extracted) for 'equalis-', 'equaliz-', 'Development Fund', 'grant', 'subsid-' turned up only the generic s.77 5%-of-rates transfer (now na-regional-councils-act-1992 -> na-local-authorities-act-1992, calculated_from) and generic 'moneys appropriated by law' language (ss.80, 33) -- no dedicated, named equalisation fund or codified allocation formula beyond the flat 5% rate-share exists in either Act.

_dropped.edge: na-nsa-cpi methodology citation to SADC Harmonised CPI / COICOP / IMF-ILO CPI Manual
_dropped.why: Reconfirms and extends na-cpi-social-protection.json's existing open question na-cpi-formula-unconfirmed using a newer (June 2026) NCPI Bulletin plus additional search paths not tried previously: nsa.org.na's CPI landing page (nsa.org.na/ncpi/, a screenshot/dashboard-embed page with no methodology text), the publications index, and the WordPress REST search API (nsa.org.na/wp-json/wp/v2/search) queried with 'CPI metadata', 'CPI concepts', 'CPI technical report', 'Namibia CPI manual', and 'COICOP' -- none returned a dedicated CPI methodology/technical document. The June 2026 bulletin's own 'Box 2: NCPI basket weights' section describes the basket in generic terms ('basket now contains over 350 items, grouped into 12 categories and 55 sub-categories', rebased in 2013 using 2009/10 NHIES data) but never names COICOP, the SADC Harmonised CPI framework, or the IMF/ILO CPI Manual anywhere in the document. See the corresponding UPDATE prepended to na-nsa-cpi's description in na-cpi-social-protection.json.

The Strategic Plan's Table 3 and risk register both name 'the Government of the Republic of Namibia' / 'the central government' as a funding/subsidy source for the City, but neither passage cites the Local Authorities Act, its s.80(1)(a) general appropriations clause, or any other specific instrument by name -- so no citation-based edge can be drawn from this document alone, even though s.80(1)(a)'s general 'moneys appropriated by law' mechanism is the plausible statutory basis.

_dropped.edge: systematic .gov.na access failure blocking MURD budget speech, OAG named local-authority audit reports, mof.gov.na, and www.gov.na
_dropped.why: Essentially every *.gov.na domain tested this round (oag.gov.na, murd.gov.na, mof.gov.na, www.gov.na, npc.gov.na on https) either TLS-reset mid-handshake or returned HTTP 503, while non-.gov.na Namibian domains (nsa.org.na, windhoekcc.org.na, lac.org.na) worked normally -- a pattern consistent with a systematic network-level block/instability affecting the .gov.na TLD from this environment, not content-level absence. Specifically blocked: MURD's Budget Speech 2025-26 FY (murd.gov.na), the Auditor-General's named local-authority audit reports whose existence is known only via search-result titles (e.g. 'REPORT OF THE AUDITOR-GENERAL ON THE ACCOUNTS OF THE ... 2013-2014 Khomas', '2013-2014 Government of Namibia', '2010-2011 Government of Namibia', all at oag.gov.na), and a Wayback Machine fallback attempt (rate-limited, then proxy-rejected). Flagged for a future round's retry, possibly at a different time of day or via an alternate egress path, before concluding these documents are genuinely inaccessible rather than technically blocked. UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round): retried murd.gov.na, oag.gov.na, mof.gov.na, and www.gov.na across ~10 attempts over ~10 minutes, both http/https, both www/bare forms -- ALL still fail, but with TWO DISTINCT failure modes: connection-reset for oag.gov.na/mof.gov.na/www.gov.na, connection-timeout for murd.gov.na. Critically, npc.gov.na now WORKS FINE this round (301 redirect to www.npc.gov.na, HTTP 200, real downloadable PDF content) -- this REFINES the prior 'systematic .gov.na block' characterization: it is NOT a blanket .gov.na TLD-level block, but a per-host issue specific to murd.gov.na/oag.gov.na/mof.gov.na/www.gov.na. The exact target URLs for both the MURD FY2025/26 budget speech and the OAG 2013-2014 Khomas local-authority audit were CONFIRMED TO EXIST via search-engine indexing (exact filenames found) but neither could be fetched due to this host-level block. A working non-.gov.na mirror, parliament.na, hosts SOME OAG material (a 2020 OAG self-audit PDF confirmed accessible), but that document is image-only/no text layer AND off-target (OAG auditing itself, not a local authority). Wayback Machine retries were inconclusive (429 rate-limiting on archive.org's own side, not a .gov.na-related failure). Recommend a future round retry murd.gov.na/oag.gov.na/mof.gov.na/www.gov.na specifically (not write off .gov.na entirely, since npc.gov.na is reachable).

_dropped.why: A government-commissioned capacity assessment of Namibia's regional councils appears to exist and to be reproduced on ResearchGate, but is hosted on an academic-paper aggregator rather than the ministry's own domain, and was not fetched or verified this round. Flagged as the best remaining non-primary lead per the fallback rule, for a future round to chase directly (or to locate a government-hosted primary copy of).
